title: Serving surface PRD: product-level requirements, packaging, and release plan (H1 2026)
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose
- This PRD defines the product surface for Redwood Inference’s hosted and dedicated serving APIs for H1 2026. It unifies the request surface, packaging options, and the coordinated release plan and pricing experiments. The goal is to improve developer productivity, make cost/latency tradeoffs explicit, and enable predictable enterprise adoption.

Scope
- Host: Redwood API (hosted + dedicated capacity).
- Features: unified inference endpoints, routing-level quality tiers, bundled latency/cost SKUs, rollout plan to customers on trial and enterprise tiers.
- Out of scope: Private on-prem installer packaging (will get a compatibility spec in a follow-up doc).

Background and motivation
- Customers report confusion between per-token pricing, dedicated commitments, and the cost/latency payoff of quantization and batching. Engineering and sales need an aligned product that: (1) exposes clear choices to developers, (2) enables reliable performance SLOs per SKU, and (3) supports cheap experimentation via feature flags.

Personas
- ML Engineer: needs predictable latency and model versioning for product features.
- Platform Engineer: wants to allocate budget across teams and enforce quotas.
- Startup founder/Developer: wants a simple price ladder and a quick path to production.
- Enterprise CS / Sales: needs SLAs and an upgrade path to dedicated capacity.

Goals (measurable)
1) Reduce upgrade friction: 30% fewer support tickets about pricing/latency choices in Q2 2026 vs Q4 2025.
2) Increase enterprise conversions: 15% lift in Dedicated leads attributable to clearer packaging by end of H1 2026.
3) Developer clarity: >90% of new signups pick a recommended SKU within first 15 minutes (post-checkout funnel metric).
4) Maintain median hosted generation latency <= 220ms for the Standard tier at 512 tokens.

Key product decisions (summary)
- Introduce three quality/latency tiers on the public API: Economy, Standard, and Premium. Each tier maps to a routing policy and default model/quantization profile.
- Offer two packaging paths: self-serve metered (per-token + tier surcharge) and committed Dedicated bundles (monthly reservation + reduced per-token).
- Feature-flagged rollout for routing fallbacks and progressive rollout to high-volume customers.

Requirements
Functional requirements (FR)
FR-01: Single POST /v1/generate endpoint with optional query param tier={economy|standard|premium}.
FR-02: Default behavior: if no tier specified, backend selects Standard.
FR-03: Tier-to-model mapping documented and editable in product config.
FR-04: SDKs (Python/Node/Go) must expose a 'preferred_tier' client option and a helper to estimate cost for a prompt.
FR-05: Admin console: ability to create packaged bundles and assign to accounts.

Non-functional requirements (NFR)
NFR-01: SLOs per tier (target):
- Economy: P95 latency <= 450ms for 256 tokens; availability 99.5%.
- Standard: P95 latency <= 220ms for 512 tokens; availability 99.9%.
- Premium: P95 latency <= 120ms for 1024 tokens; availability 99.95%.
NFR-02: Price estimation API must respond <= 40ms 95% of the time.
NFR-03: Pricing and tier selection controls in the console must load within 1.5s on a 100ms RTT network.
NFR-04: Rollout system must support canary at 0.5%, 1%, 5%, 25%, 100% and automatic rollback based on error budget triggers.

Acceptance criteria (AC)
- AC-01: Integration tests demonstrate endpoint with tier parameter routes to expected model and returns tokens with stream support in SDKs.
- AC-02: Benchmarked invoices: cost estimator matches actual per-token billing within 3% on test billing runs.
- AC-03: Performance tests show Standard tier meets NFR-01 in the staging environment with production-like hardware.
- AC-04: Admin console can provision a Dedicated bundle and enforce quota isolation for a test account.

Design notes
Routing and policy
- Each incoming request is annotated with tier metadata and hashed to routing bucketing. A policy engine (policyd) decides model variant, region preference, and fallback sequence.
- Fallback order example for Standard: Standard-quantized -> Standard-full -> Economy-quantized (if compatibility). Fallback policies are versioned and controlled by flags.

Model/quantization mapping (recommended default)
| Tier | Model family | Quantization | Target hardware |
| Economy | open-m-7b | int8/4 | cpu-burst/gpu-low |
| Standard | open-m-13b | int8 | A10/A16 or comparable |
| Premium | open-m-70b | fp16 | H100/V100-style fast GPUs |

Pricing and packaging (product recommendation)
- Metered (public): base per-token unit + tier multiplier for latency premium. Example (proposal for experiment):
  - Tokens unit: $0.0008 / 1k tokens (base).
  - Economy multiplier: x0.8 (cheaper inference but higher latency).
  - Standard multiplier: x1.0 (base).
  - Premium multiplier: x2.5 (fast path and priority routing).
- Dedicated bundles: monthly reservation tiers with discounted included units and overage rates. Example bundle table:
| Bundle | Monthly commitment | Included tokens | Effective per-1k price (if used fully) | Notes |
| Dev  | $2,500 | 400M tokens | $0.0006 | For small teams, limited to Standard tier |
| Growth | $12,000 | 2.5B tokens | $0.00048 | Optional burst capacity into Premium at +30% surcharge |
| Enterprise | $60,000 | 15B tokens | $0.00035 | SLA 99.95% and named support engineer |
- Upsell mechanics: free trial credits for Premium trials (30M tokens) and automated usage report highlighting latency/cost tradeoffs after 7 days.

Billing and metering details (implementation notes)
- Metering window: per-request token counts + model variant metadata. Billing pipeline must tag events with tier and bundle_id.
- Rate limiting: default per-account QPS for Standard = 50 requests/sec. Dedicated bundles may assign higher QPS and token concurrency.

Rollout plan and timeline (Q1–Q2 2026)
1) Pilot (Q1 start, 6 weeks): enable tier param in API and SDKs for internal feature teams and 3 external pilot customers. Collect latency and cost telemetry. Owner: Product + Eng Platform.
2) Closed beta (Q1 mid, 4 weeks): open to selected self-serve signups with dedicated dashboard and billing telemetry. Owner: Product, SRE.
3) Pricing experiment (Q1 end – Q2 start, 8 weeks): run A/B experiment comparing per-token multiplier vs flat price tiers to measure conversion and revenue impact. Owner: Growth & Finance.
4) Public launch (Q2): full documentation, console UI, marketing materials, and gradual rollout for all new signups. Owner: Product + GTM.

Canary and rollback rules
- Canary cohorts: 0.5% internal -> 1% alpha customers -> 5% early adopters -> 25% general -> 100%.
- Automatic rollback triggers: error rate spike > 2x baseline OR P95 latency breach for tier beyond configured SLO for > 10 minutes.

SDK and docs deliverables
- SDK updates: Python/Node/Go: new Client.preferred_tier option, cost_estimate(prompt, length), and sample code for migration.
- Docs: tutorial ‘Picking the right tier’, developer FAQ comparing cost/latency, migration checklist for Dedicated customers.

Release notes (initial public launch summary)
- Feature: tiered inference surface with Economy / Standard / Premium options.
- Admin: Console support for Dedicated bundle provisioning and visibility into tier-level token consumption.
- SDK: new stable API for preferred_tier and cost estimation.
- Known limitations: Private on-prem packaging not included; quantization profiles for specific open models require additional validation and may vary by hardware.

Operational runbook highlights
- Monitoring: per-tier dashboards (latency, error rates, churned requests, routing fallbacks).
- Alerting: Tier-SLO breaches -> P1 paged to on-call SRE; billing mismatch alerts -> PagerDuty to FinOps.
- Escalation: CS lead to product -> Eng runtime -> SRE.

Ownership and stakeholders
- Product Owner: Maya Chen (product).
- Engineering: Runtime (owner: Ravi Kapoor), Platform (owner: Sara Kim).
- Sales/GTM: Lead: Anika Patel.
- Finance: Billing integration owner: Marcus Lee.

Risks and mitigations
- Risk: Customers misinterpret tier differences and overpay for Premium needlessly. Mitigation: default recs in console, 7-day usage report, in-app estimator.
- Risk: Pricing experiment reduces revenue if discounts are too aggressive. Mitigation: conservative initial discounts, close monitoring, and finance kill-switch in experiment.
- Risk: Performance variability across regions. Mitigation: regional SLOs and auto-fallback region policy.

Appendix A — Example API usage
- Example request (curl):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"prompt": "Summarize the following customer support ticket...", "max_tokens": 300, "tier": "premium"}'

- Example SDK (Python):
  from redwood import Client
  client = Client(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_KEY'), preferred_tier='standard')
  estimate = client.cost_estimate(prompt, max_tokens=512)
  resp = client.generate(prompt, max_tokens=512)

Appendix B — Acceptance test checklist
- End-to-end test that verifies token meter tags with tier metadata.
- Load test at standard 2x production expected peak to validate autoscale.
- Billing reconciliation run to ensure estimator accuracy.

Appendix C — Metrics to track (initial)
- Tier selection rate (percent of requests specifying tier).
- Conversion rate from Standard -> Dedicated within 90 days of signup.
- Median & P95 latency by tier and region.
- Revenue per 1k tokens by bundle and metered customers.

Next steps and actions (immediate)
- Product: finalize multiplier values with Finance by 2026-01-20.
- Eng: implement /v1/generate tier param and SDK changes (sprint 2026-01-22 -> 2026-02-19).
- SRE: prepare staging workload to validate NFRs (ready by 2026-02-01).

If you are reviewing: please comment with any objections to the proposed multipliers or the rollout schedule. For design questions, ping Ravi Kapoor; for pricing/finance, ping Marcus Lee.
